title: Make the repo agent-ready
summary: Turn the codebase into ground an AI agent can actually work: write the AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md conventions, install an agent-skills stack, wire one-line lint/typecheck/test commands, connect MCP servers for your vendors, and prove it by having an agent ship a small fix end-to-end.

parts.title: Audit the repo (docs, build, test entry points)
parts.guidance: Try the repository as a new contributor: locate setup instructions, the pinned runtime and package manager, generated files and CI commands. Run the permitted local checks and identify missing configuration, undocumented prerequisites and failures already present. Follow one small feature or bug through the source to see which checks cover it. Return file references and command results for the gaps that would stop an agent from making and verifying a bounded change.

parts.title: Write the AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md conventions
parts.guidance: Write instructions using commands and conventions verified in the audit. Explain where code lives, which files are generated, how to run focused checks and how changes reach review. Reference existing rules for secrets and external effects, including authority already delegated for routine work. Keep tool-specific files consistent with the clients that read them. Test the instructions in a fresh session and fix the places where the reader must guess a command or hidden prerequisite.

parts.title: Install an agent-skills stack
parts.guidance: Pick a skill for a demonstrated task the repository needs help with. Read its instructions, installation behavior and dependencies before adding it, checking compatibility with the chosen agent. Install in the intended local or repository scope and trial a harmless example. Any added credential access or external permission needs the responsible owner's authority. Keep the source/version and removal path, and discard skills that conflict with repository rules or add no useful behavior.

parts.title: Wire one-line lint, typecheck, and test commands
parts.guidance: Expose the repository's lint, type-check and test paths as commands that work from the documented setup. Check their exit status by running a passing case and a controlled failure, then remove the deliberate failure. Offer a focused command for a small change alongside the required broader gates. Document existing failures and necessary test fixtures so an agent can tell a regression from a broken baseline.

parts.title: Connect MCP servers for the stack’s vendors
parts.guidance: Connect only the vendor tasks the agent actually needs, using the verified server and the runtime's supported setup. Check the account and granted scopes against the service owner's authorization, then try a harmless read whose result can be independently confirmed. Inspect the tools actually exposed and test the operations the workflow will use. Protect credentials, keep revocation available and define which external writes require separate case-specific authority.

parts.title: Trial run: an agent ships a small fix end-to-end
parts.guidance: Give an agent a small bug with a reproducible failure and expected fix, using the new repository instructions as its starting point. Watch where setup, checks or missing context force it to guess. Review the patch and test result, then carry it through the normal review and release path only as far as the task authorizes. Fix the instructions from the friction actually observed and keep the example available for the next contributor.

parts.title: Team review of guardrails and permissions
parts.guidance: Review what the trial actually accessed and changed. Decide which routine tasks can proceed under standing delegation and which need a case-specific decision, especially production changes, external messages and access to company data. Check who owns credentials, can revoke access and handles unexpected behavior. The responsible owners set those boundaries in the configuration and repository policy; use another small trial to test any boundary that remains ambiguous.

metadata.supportReason: This is the one process agents run on themselves end-to-end — audit, docs, skills, checks, and the proving fix are all agent work. Only the guardrail review is a team call.
